CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acute back pain with right lower extremity paresthesias

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with acute onset low back pain and right lower extremity paresthesias. While raking leaves yesterday afternoon, he developed back tightening and pins-and-needles sensation in his right foot approximately 2 hours after returning indoors. Home treatment with ice and ibuprofen provided no relief. Heat and sitting improve symptoms. Pain occurs with lumbar flexion but not extension. He reports a similar episode 3 years prior that resolved spontaneously within one day. He denies regular physical activity.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for paresthesias in right lower extremity. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain (resolved), episode 3 years prior

MEDICATIONS
No regular medications

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Denies regular physical activity. Does not routinely perform yard work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic: Dorsiflexion strength normal bilaterally. Lower extremity pulses equal and intact bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Lumbar spine tender to palpation at L5. Pain with lumbar flexion. No pain with lumbar extension.

RESULTS
X-ray of lumbar spine: Normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute low back strain with right lower extremity paresthesias

Plan:
1. Activity modification and rest
2. Meloxicam prescribed for pain and inflammation management
3. Physical therapy referral for stretching, strengthening exercises, and conditioning
4. Follow-up in 2 weeks
5. MRI of lumbar spine if symptoms persist after 2 weeks
